quests.instruction: Below the ground floor, the family stores old furniture and does the laundry in a room that stays cool all summer. Which room is this?
quests.question: Basement
quests.hint: This storage room sits below the rest of the house, often underground.
quests.explanation: That's right! A basement sits below the ground floor and stays cool, perfect for storage.
quests.funFact: Some basements are turned into a cozy extra playroom or movie room.

quests.instruction: To make the wooden chair softer to sit on, Mei added a small, squishy pillow to the seat. What did she add?
quests.question: Cushion
quests.hint: This soft, squishy pillow makes a chair or sofa more comfortable.
quests.explanation: Yes! A cushion is a soft, squishy pillow that makes a seat more comfortable.
quests.funFact: Many sofas are decorated with several colorful cushions.

quests.instruction: Looking straight up inside the living room, Tomás noticed a fan hanging from the flat surface above his head. What is this surface called?
quests.question: Ceiling
quests.hint: This is the flat surface above your head, right below the roof.
quests.explanation: Correct! A ceiling is the flat surface above your head, right below the roof.
quests.funFact: Some ceilings have a light or a fan hanging right in the middle.

quests.instruction: After a big family dinner, a stack of dirty plates and cups needs washing. Which kitchen appliance can clean them all without any scrubbing by hand?
quests.question: Dishwasher
quests.hint: This large appliance sprays water and soap to clean stacks of dishes.
quests.explanation: That's right! A dishwasher sprays water and soap to clean a whole stack of dirty dishes.
quests.funFact: Before dishwashers were invented, every dish had to be scrubbed clean by hand.

quests.instruction: Before stepping inside, Grandpa likes to sit outside near the front door and wave at neighbors walking by. Which part of the home is he sitting on?
quests.question: Porch
quests.hint: This outdoor space is right by the front door, often with a chair or two.
quests.explanation: Yes! A porch is the outdoor space near the front door, perfect for waving at neighbors.
quests.funFact: Many families keep a welcome mat and a chair or two out on the porch.

quests.instruction: A delivery worker left a small package right on the flat step outside the front door. Where exactly was it left?
quests.question: Doorstep
quests.hint: This is the very last step you take before walking through the front door.
quests.explanation: Correct! A doorstep is the flat step right outside the front door, a common spot for packages.
quests.funFact: Packages are sometimes left right on the doorstep for someone to bring inside.

quests.instruction: Tired after a long day, Elena gets into her pajamas and climbs into bed to sleep for the night. Which room is she in?
quests.question: Bedroom
quests.hint: This room has a bed and is usually the quietest room in the house.
quests.explanation: That's right! A bedroom has a bed and is where we sleep for the night.
quests.funFact: Most people spend around eight hours every night sleeping in their bedroom.

quests.instruction: Living far from her grandmother, Zara picks up a device and speaks into it so she can hear Grandma's voice. Which device is she using?
quests.question: Telephone
quests.hint: You pick up this device and speak into it to talk with someone far away.
quests.explanation: Yes! A telephone lets you talk with and hear someone even if they live far away.
quests.funFact: The very first telephones were connected to the wall by a long, curly cord.

quests.instruction: After spilling juice, Dad wipes up the mess from the surface right under everyone's feet. Which surface is he cleaning?
quests.question: Floor
quests.hint: This is the flat surface under your feet in every room.
quests.explanation: Correct! A floor is the flat surface under your feet, and it needs wiping when something spills.
quests.funFact: A floor can be covered in wood, tile, or soft carpet depending on the room.

quests.instruction: Piles of dirty clothes are sorted into light and dark colors before going into the washing machine. Which room is this happening in?
quests.question: Laundry Room
quests.hint: This room usually has a washing machine and sometimes a dryer too.
quests.explanation: That's right! A laundry room is where clothes are sorted and washed clean.
quests.funFact: Many families sort clothes into light and dark piles before washing them.

quests.instruction: Checking the numbers on the wall, the whole family realizes it is almost time for dinner. What are they checking?
quests.question: Clock
quests.hint: This object has hands or numbers that show what time it is.
quests.explanation: Yes! A clock shows the time, helping the family know when dinner is ready.
quests.funFact: Checking a clock helps everyone in the family know when it is time for dinner or bed.

quests.instruction: A refrigerator, a toaster, and a washing machine all share one thing in common: they use electricity to help with jobs like cooking or cleaning. What do we call machines like these?
quests.question: Appliance
quests.hint: This word describes any electric machine that helps with a job at home.
quests.explanation: Correct! An appliance is any machine that uses electricity to help with a job like cooking or cleaning.
quests.funFact: Most appliances need to be plugged into an electrical outlet to work.

quests.instruction: Walking straight from the bedroom to the kitchen without stepping up or down, Sofia passes family photos on the wall. Which part of the home is she walking through?
quests.question: Hallway
quests.hint: This flat passage connects rooms on the same floor.
quests.explanation: That's right! A hallway is a flat passage connecting rooms on the same floor.
quests.funFact: A hallway connects rooms together, almost like a little indoor path.

quests.instruction: In a hurry before soccer practice, Leo warms up his leftovers in just one minute using a quick kitchen appliance. Which one is he using?
quests.question: Microwave
quests.hint: This small appliance warms food quickly at the push of a button.
quests.explanation: Yes! A microwave warms up leftovers quickly at just the push of a button.
quests.funFact: You should never put metal spoons or forks inside a microwave while it runs.

quests.instruction: On a hot summer afternoon, a spinning machine with blades pushes a cool breeze across the room. What is this machine called?
quests.question: Fan
quests.hint: This machine spins with blades to push air and cool a room.
quests.explanation: Correct! A fan spins with blades to push a cool breeze across a room.
quests.funFact: A fan does not actually cool the air, but the breeze it makes helps you feel cooler.

quests.instruction: Snow falls all winter, but it slides right off the slanted top of the house instead of soaking through. What part of the house protects the family this way?
quests.question: Roof
quests.hint: This is the top covering of a house that keeps out rain and snow.
quests.explanation: That's right! A roof is the top covering of a house that keeps out rain and snow.
quests.funFact: A roof is slanted on many houses so rain and snow slide right off.

quests.instruction: Every morning, Aiden opens a drawer in a wide piece of furniture to grab a clean pair of socks. Which furniture is he using?
quests.question: Dresser
quests.hint: This wide furniture piece has several drawers for folded clothes.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dresser has drawers for folded clothes, like socks, shirts, and pants.
quests.funFact: Many people place a mirror right on top of their dresser.

quests.instruction: Bright morning sunlight shines through a glass opening in the wall, waking Camila up gently. Which part of the room let the light in?
quests.question: Window
quests.hint: This glass opening in the wall lets in sunlight and can be opened for fresh air.
quests.explanation: Correct! A window is the glass opening that lets sunlight and fresh air into a room.
quests.funFact: Many windows can be opened to let fresh air blow into the room.

quests.instruction: The person who lives in the house right next door waved and said good morning while watering her flowers. What do we call this person?
quests.question: Neighbor
quests.hint: This word describes someone who lives close by, right next door.
quests.explanation: That's right! A neighbor is someone who lives close by, like right next door.
quests.funFact: Waving or saying hello is a friendly way to greet a neighbor.

quests.instruction: After a muddy day outside, Ravi fills a large basin with warm water so he can sit and soak clean from head to toe. Which fixture is he using?
quests.question: Bathtub
quests.hint: This fixture fills with water so you can sit inside and soak.
quests.explanation: Yes! A bathtub fills with warm water so you can sit and soak clean.
quests.funFact: Some bathtubs have bubbles or rubber ducks to make bath time extra fun.

quests.instruction: Every December, the family climbs up to the very top of the house to bring down boxes of holiday decorations. Which room are they visiting?
quests.question: Attic
quests.hint: This storage room sits right under the roof, at the very top of the house.
quests.explanation: Correct! An attic sits right under the roof, a common spot for storing holiday decorations.
quests.funFact: Many families store their holiday decorations in the attic until it is time to use them again.

quests.instruction: Spreading out her pencils, books, and papers, Yuki sits down at a sturdy flat surface to finish her homework. Which piece of furniture is she using?
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: This flat furniture piece is used for writing, drawing, or homework.
quests.explanation: That's right! A desk is a flat piece of furniture made for writing and homework.
quests.funFact: Many students keep pencils, books, and papers neatly on their desk.

quests.instruction: Before playing catch in the fenced yard, Marcus makes sure to close the small door built into the fence behind him. What did he close?
quests.question: Gate
quests.hint: This small door is built right into a fence, not into the house.
quests.explanation: Yes! A gate is a small door built into a fence, and closing it keeps pets and toys safely inside.
quests.funFact: Many gates have a latch to keep them closed until someone opens it.

quests.instruction: Standing at the front door with her hands full of groceries, Aisha still needs one small metal tool to unlock it. What is she reaching for?
quests.question: Key
quests.hint: This small metal tool turns inside a lock to open a door.
quests.explanation: Correct! A key is the small metal tool that turns inside a lock to open a door.
quests.funFact: A key has to match its lock exactly, or the door will not open.

quests.instruction: On a chilly night, Emily pulls a large piece of soft fabric over herself in bed to stay warm while she sleeps. What is she using?
quests.question: Blanket
quests.hint: This soft cover keeps you warm while you sleep at night.
quests.explanation: That's right! A blanket is the soft cover that keeps you warm while you sleep.
quests.funFact: Many people keep an extra blanket nearby for chilly winter nights.

quests.instruction: After using the bathroom, Diego makes sure to flush the water and wash his hands right after. Which fixture did he just flush?
quests.question: Toilet
quests.hint: This bathroom fixture flushes water away when you are finished using it.
quests.explanation: Yes! A toilet flushes water away, and washing your hands afterward is always a healthy habit.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands after using the toilet is one of the best ways to stay healthy.

quests.instruction: Kicking a ball across the open grass beside their house, the twins laugh and chase after it together. Which outdoor space are they playing in?
quests.question: Yard
quests.hint: This open, grassy space is perfect for playing games outside.
quests.explanation: Correct! A yard is the open, grassy space around a home, perfect for playing games.
quests.funFact: A big yard gives kids plenty of room to run, play, and kick a ball.

quests.instruction: Moving into their brand new, completely empty home, the Diaz family orders beds, tables, chairs, and a sofa to fill every room. What is the general word for all these movable items?
quests.question: Furniture
quests.hint: This is the general word for beds, tables, chairs, and sofas together.
quests.explanation: That's right! Furniture is the general word for movable items like beds, tables, and chairs.
quests.funFact: Furniture can be made from wood, metal, plastic, or even soft fabric.

quests.instruction: Between the stove, the oven, the refrigerator, and the sink, this room has more appliances working together than any other room in the whole house. Which room is it?
quests.question: Kitchen
quests.hint: This room has a stove, an oven, a refrigerator, and a sink, all in one place.
quests.explanation: Yes! The Kitchen holds more appliances than any other room, all working together to make meals.
quests.funFact: Kitchens usually have more appliances than any other room in the house.

quests.instruction: From the smallest chore to the biggest birthday dinner, every single person sharing this one home works together as a team. What word describes this whole group?
quests.question: Household
quests.hint: Think of the word that groups every family member living under one roof together.
quests.explanation: Correct! A household is everyone who lives together, sharing chores, meals, and one home.
quests.funFact: Every household usually shares chores like cooking, cleaning, and tidying up.
